message.content: The main attack surface here is the truncated decimal coefficients against a 1e-6 absolute tolerance over the full finite FP16 domain. I'll record concrete, testable claims for the experimenter.

function.arguments: {"rationale": "The coefficients are rounded to only 3-5 significant decimal digits (e.g. -122.9, 485.4, 24.86, 0.66) while the contract demands 1e-6 absolute accuracy. message.reasoning_content:
Record 2-3 in-scope claims: coefficient truncation accuracy; FP32 rounding accumulation near large |x| where local_angle approaches π/4 (catastrophic-ish? angle+local in FP32 ~ 1.57 with ulp ~1.2e-7, fine); boundary at 0.66 threshold vs Cephes' actual threshold (Cephes uses 0.66? For atan double, thresholds are MAXNUM? Cephes atan uses x > 2.414 and x > 0.66? Actually Cephes atan: if x > 2.414 uses angle=pi/2, x -= 1/x; else if x > 0.66 uses (x-1)/(x+1), pi/4; else x, 0. So thresholds match; but coefficients truncated to ~4 digits vs Cephes doubles with full precision). Primary claim: max abs error > 1e-6 somewhere, e.g., near z^2 midrange in middle branch. Also boundary mismatch at 0.66 FP32: middle branch error could peak at boundary where z largest? z for middle branch ranges up to (2.414-1)/(2.414+1)=0.4142; z^2 up to ~0.1716. For lower branch z up to 0.66. Rational error at z=0.66: polynomial fit for [0, 0.66]? Cephes coefficients designed for z up to tan(pi/12)? Actually lower branch z ≤ 0.66 gives atan up to 0.58 rad; Cephes rational is fit over z∈[0,0.66]. Truncation error could exceed 1e-6 at boundary.

Record 3 claims: (1) truncated-coefficient approximation error exceeds 1e-6 somewhere in domain (in_scope); (2) FP32 rounding: middle branch output ~π/2 - small; rounding of angle+local in FP32 gives error up to ~1 ulp of 1.57 ≈ 1.2e-7, within tolerance — but combined with truncation could push over; maybe scope as separate claim about cumulative FP32 rounding for large |x| approaching π/2 with output ulp ~1.19e-7, need total ≤1e-6 — plausibly fine. Keep it as second claim anyway since budget is tight. (3) threshold: exact tie at |x| slightly above 2.414213562373095: FP32 constant comparison fine.

Better third: exhaustive FP16 domain sweep would find worst case — but claims must describe conditions. I'll record two strong claims plus one about near-boundary 0.66 region specifically.
